title: Python for networking: Netmiko, NAPALM, Nornir and Paramiko

videos.script: Four Python libraries do most of the work of network automation, and each one sits on the one below it. {{layers}} Paramiko is SSH, and nothing more. It opens a connection and runs a command. {{paramiko}} Netmiko knows the device: its prompt, its paging, its configuration mode. It is also where a refused command can pass unnoticed, unless you tell it what a refusal looks like. {{netmiko}} NAPALM puts the same methods over every vendor. You load a configuration, look at the difference, commit it, and roll it back. {{napalm}} And Nornir runs a task on many devices at once, from an inventory kept as data. One device failing does not stop the others. {{nornir}} In this lesson you use all four against the lab's routers, and you see why asking a router for JSON beats reading its screen. {{json}}
